leadReason: Accept the exact Indonesian proposal. Both reviewers accept all thirteen disputed units and find no additional defect. terminologyDecisions.relativeTime: Use count-unit-lagi for future intervals and count-unit-yang-lalu for past intervals.
terminologyDecisions.memberSample: Use sampel for a member subset and anggota in every count category.
terminologyDecisions.obligation: Use an explicit harus size clause for the Mermaid ceiling. A nominal maximum is understandable in this instruction context, but the full clause is clearer.
terminologyDecisions.references: Keep the defined ref term for stable comment/thread lookup identifiers. Rujukan and referensi remain clear ordinary words for references in the other descriptions; protocol property names remain exact.
terminologyDecisions.narration: Use saya for participant narration and Anda only where the addressee needs to be named.

terminologyReview: Guideline clarification: the revised distinction in references/common.md and references/ga.md is correct. The evidence agrees on three points. intl-workerd.json shows Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat unsupported (English output) for eo, be and ga, while Intl.PluralRules returns native categories for all 18 locales. InstructionTemplates (packages/shared/src/instruction-template.ts) builds Intl.PluralRules for the content language and throws when a catalog omits a native count variant or a message. BotText.andList and transcriptLabelList join items only through the catalog's formatting.* patterns. So Bickr's own formatters never 'silently return English'; the English fallback is only a property of the platform Intl list and relative-time formatters, which Bickr does not use for these strings. One leftover: references/eo.md line 7 still says 'The runtime formatters silently return English, although plural rules work.' It should use the same wording as common.md and ga.md (be.md already does). This is a guideline edit only and changes no frozen English unit.

Indonesian terminology follows the lead decisions. Relative time uses "N … lagi" and "N … yang lalu" (no "dalam N" or interval sentence left). "sampel" names the member subset and "anggota" stays unmarked in every count. Required maximums use "harus … paling banyak" and capacities use "dapat memuat paling banyak", so the modal force follows the source. "saya" is used for narration, and "Anda" only where the addressee needs naming. "ref" stays the defined lookup term, with "rujukan" or "referensi" for ordinary prose references.

grok.terminologyReview: The revised Workers boundary is correct. Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat fall back to English for Esperanto, Belarusian, and Irish, while Intl.PluralRules supports native categories. Bickr catalog formatters use explicit translated patterns and reject a missing entry, so the older phrase that runtime formatters silently return English does not describe Bickr. Indonesian is outside that fallback set. Indonesian has only other, and a noun after a numeral stays singular. Future time uses count-unit lagi, which does not carry the within reading of dalam. Past time uses count-unit yang lalu. harus states the Mermaid must ceiling. dapat memuat paling banyak stays a can-limit. Jaga ... dalam batas stays the keep-within instruction. anggota is the member noun at every count. sampel is a subset, not an example. ref stays the stable lookup term. rujukan and referensi in other descriptions are ordinary words and are not an open question. Narration uses saya. Anda appears only where the addressee is named.

previousDecision.leadReason: State the Mermaid size rule explicitly with harus berukuran paling banyak. The original nominal maximum already gives a bound in an instructional context, so I reject the claim that it necessarily removes the rule. The new full clause makes the obligation plain and preserves the fence, label, configuration/frontmatter bans, and all other instructions.
previousDecision.candidateReason: Opus best preserves autonomous, unsociable and villain meanings. Codex says independent, Grok says acting alone and misstates escapes, and Gemini changes voting to choosing. Correct duplicate-only scope, recent timing and private memory.
previousDecision.opusReason: Every line checked: notice limits, autonomy, role meanings, decisions, activities, audience, follow rules, JSON and quoting, refs, duplicate replies, Markdown, Mermaid, SVG and math limits, ‼️ precedence, persona fields and style and length rules are preserved; Anda is used where the actor needs it.
previousDecision.grokReason: Mermaid source must be at most {{mermaidKiB}} KiB. The bare paling banyak phrase drops harus. harus berukuran paling banyak restores the obligation and the size verb. opus.reason: I accepted the nominal "paling banyak" originally. I agree with the lead that it already bounded the size in this instruction context, so Grok's claim that it dropped the rule overstates the defect. "Sumber Mermaid harus berukuran paling banyak N KiB" states the obligation explicitly and matches the structured-output maximums ("harus berisi paling banyak"). The fence, label and configuration ban are unchanged.

SVG and math still say Jaga ... dalam batas, which matches Keep ... within. KiB stays. The rest of the instruction is unchanged.
